source.title: Subexponential parameterized directed Steiner network problems on planar graphs: a complete classification

accepted.question_text: For a class D of directed demand graphs closed under transitive equivalence and identifying vertices, consider Planar D-Steiner Network: the input is a planar digraph G, a set T of k terminals, and a demand digraph D in D on vertex set T, and the objective is to find a minimum-edge subgraph H of G such that every demand edge (u, v) in D is realized by a directed u-to-v path in H. Are there choices of D for which Planar D-Steiner Network is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by k even though the corresponding D-Steiner Network problem on general digraphs is W[1]-hard?

evidence.quote: D-Steiner Network Input: Digraph G, a set of k terminals T ⊆ V (G), and a demand digraph D ∈ D with vertex set T. Question: What is the minimum number of edges in a subgraph H of G where for each (u, v) ∈ E(D) there is a u → v path in H?

In light of Theorem 1.1 and the earlier results on planar graphs, there are three natural questions that arise: 1. Are there cases that are FPT on planar graphs, but W[1]-hard on general graphs? ... We answer the first question negatively: the hard cases remain hard on planar graphs.

accepted.question_text: For Planar D-Steiner Network with parameter k equal to the number of terminals, where D is a class of directed demand graphs closed under transitive equivalence and identifying vertices and the task is to satisfy every demand edge by a directed path in a minimum-edge planar subgraph, are there nontrivial fixed-parameter tractable cases whose running time is subexponential in k, specifically 2^{o(k)} n^{O(1)}?

evidence.quote: In light of Theorem 1.1 and the earlier results on planar graphs, there are three natural questions that arise: ... 2. Are there subexponential FPT cases on planar graphs, that is, where the running time is 2 o(k) · n O(1)?

The answer to the second question is also negative: we show that every (nontrivial) case of Planar D-SN is at least as hard as Directed Steiner Tree, hence a known lower bound [27] shows that there is no subexponential FPT algorithm, assuming ETH.

accepted.question_text: For Planar D-Steiner Network parameterized by the number k of terminals, where D ranges over classes of directed demand graphs closed under transitive equivalence and identifying vertices, what combinatorial condition separates the cases solvable in time f(k) n^{O(sqrt(k))} from the cases for which only f(k) n^{O(k)} time is possible under ETH?
accepted.context_brief: Boundary between square-root and linear exponents

evidence.quote: 3. Where is the boundary line between the f(k) · n O( sqrt k) and f(k) · nO(k) cases?

To answer the third question, we define a finite number κ ≤ 10000 of classes Ci, i ∈ [κ], and show that these are precisely the classes of patterns that prevent subexponential f(k) · n O( sqrt k) time algorithms.
